title: Mercedes-Benz G500 4×4²

{{Short description|Off-road vehicle}}
[[File:Mercedes-Benz G 4x4-2 - prawy bok (MSP17).jpg|300px|thumb|Mercedes G500 / G550 4×4²]]

The '''Mercedes-Benz G500 4×4²''' (or '''G550 4×4²''' in the United States and Canada) is a special edition of the W-463 [[Mercedes-Benz G-Class]] (1990–2018), built with [[portal axle|portal gear axles]] and much larger wheels and tires, for greatly increased off-road capability. In production since 2015, the model combines the body of a regular long-wheelbase Mercedes G-Class with the portal axles with hub gearing of the much larger [[Mercedes-Benz G63 AMG 6x6]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mercedes-Benz G500 4×4 previewed |url=http://www.inautonews.com/mercedes-benz-g500-4x4-previewed |website=www.inautonews.com |accessdate=22 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220090217/http://www.inautonews.com/mercedes-benz-g500-4x4-previewed |archive-date=20 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In addition to the greatly increased ground clearance, the G500 4×4² version has a significantly wider track than regular G-Class models.<ref name=CnDprotoDrive>[https://www.caranddriver.com/reviews/mercedes-benz-g500-4x4-prototype-drive-review Mercedes-Benz G500 4x4² Prototype Drive – Review – Car and Driver]</ref>

Fitted with a twin-turbo [[V8 engine]] with up to 416 HP, the vehicle stands out by combining [[Humvee]]-like off-road specifications with [[sports car]] performance, as well as being one of the very few production cars equipped with portal axles / geared hubs.

==History==
[[File:G500 4x42, Frankfurt am Main (LRM 20220129 154953).jpg|thumb|left|G500 4×4² in Frankfurt, Germany;the portal axle gives a distinct look because the axle does not align with the center of wheel]]
[[File:2017 Mercedes-Benz G550 4X4² in designo Manufaktur Mystic White, front right.jpg|thumb|US-market Mercedes-Benz G550 4X4², with some [[Brabus]] trim]]
[[File:Mercedes-Benz G500 4x4² (52573777549).jpg|thumb|G500 4×4² in France, 2019]]
[[File:Brabus 850 4X4² Final Edition (50840060343).jpg|thumb|Aftermarket version of this model, the Brabus 850 4X4² Final Edition at French autoshow in 2019]]
Mercedes-Benz initially showed the G500 4×4² to the public as a [[concept car]], called "'''Extreme-G'''". One reason the concept was developed was due to the high demand for the G-Class — in 2014 the G-Class sold over 14,000 units. As a result, a considerable budget for low-volume derivatives was authorized.<ref name=CnDprotoDrive/> Positive response to this show car helped endorse the development of a series production version.<ref>[https://www.mercedes-benz.com/en/mercedes-benz/vehicles/passenger-cars/g-class/the-mercedes-benz-g-500-4x4²-enters-series-production/ The Mercedes-Benz G-Class G500 4x4²: Max. Offroad Performance]</ref> The car was launched at the [[Geneva motor show]] and brought into production in 2015 <ref>{{cite news|title=Mercedes G 500 4x4 Concept details emerges|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cd/mercedes-g-500-4x4-concept-details-emerges-115022100646_1.html|accessdate=22 February 2015|publisher=Business Standard}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=First drive: Mercedes G500 4x4²|url=http://www.topgear.com/uk/car-news/mercedes-benz-g-wagen-g500-4-4-squared-2015-02-20|publisher=Top Gear|accessdate=22 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mercedes G500 4x4² (2015): the ultimate off-roader?|url=http://www.carmagazine.co.uk/car-news/first-official-pictures/mercedes-benz/mercedes-g500-4x4-2015-the-ultimate-off-roader/|publisher=Car Magazine UK|accessdate=22 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=More details on Mercedes G 500 4×4² concept revealed|url=http://www.arodmercedesbenz.com/more-details-on-mercedes-g-500-4x4²-concept-revealed.html |archivedate=2018-02-10 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210114928/http://www.arodmercedesbenz.com/more-details-on-mercedes-g-500-4x4%C2%B2-concept-revealed.html |publisher=Arod Mercedes-Benz|accessdate=22 February 2015}}</ref>

Though initially not available, the car was introduced to the U.S. market as a 2017 model{{nbsp}}– called the ''G550'' 4x4²{{nbsp}}– at an introduction price around $200,000.<ref name=CnDblogSQ>[http://blog.caranddriver.com/room-for-squareds-2017-mercedes-benz-g550-4x4%C2%B2-now-for-u-s-sale/ 2017 Mercedes-Benz G550 4x4² Now for U.S. Sale – News – Car and Driver Blog]</ref> In spite of the difference in designation, it has the same [[drivetrain]] as the global version.

It was also sold in Canada under the same name, and this model was part of the G-class range of models at the time which included the G550, G550 4x4<sup>2</sup> (portal axle), and G 63 (supercharged V8), and G 65 (twin turbo V-12).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-10-19 |title=Mercedes-AMG G 65 Final Edition: The Brute Retires |url=https://www.guideautoweb.com/en/articles/44450/ |access-date=2024-05-14 |website=The Car Guide |language=en}}</ref>

==Features and specifications==

The Mercedes-Benz G500 4×4² has a {{convert|4.0|L|cuin|0|abbr=on}} twin-turbo V8 [[petrol engine]] producing 416 bhp and {{convert|450|lbft|Nm|0|abbr=on}} of torque, a seven-speed [[automatic transmission]], and three lockable differentials, like any regular G-Class.<ref name=CnDblogSQ/> The special portal axles, geared hubs, and wheels are complemented by raised suspension developed by [[KW automotive|KW]] with dual spring and shock damper struts with adjustable damping, on each corner.<ref>[https://www.motor1.com/news/92246/mercedes-benz-g-500-4x4-squared-concept/ Mercedes-Benz G 500 4x4 Squared Concept]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wright |first=Micah |date=2018-09-14 |title=Mercedes-Benz G550 4x4 Squared review: Life exaggerated |url=http://autoweek.com/drives/a1707011/mercedes-benz-g550-4x4-2-review-life-exaggerated/ |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=Autoweek |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-03-15 |title=25 years KW – the history of KW |url=https://blog-int.kwautomotive.net/25-years-kw-the-history-of-kw/ |access-date=2023-03-20 |website=KW Automotive Blog |language=en-US}}</ref> The car features very aggressive styling, using a front fascia copied from the G63 and G65 AMG with dual side-pipe exhausts that exit ahead of the rear wheels on both flanks.<ref name=CnDprotoDrive/> The vehicle's ground clearance of {{convert|410|mm|in|1|abbr=on}}, which is less than the 18.2 inches that the M1165 [[Humvee]] has, but it can sprint from naught to {{convert|60|mph|km/h|0|abbr=on}} in less than six seconds.<ref name=CnDblogSQ/> On the inside, the car offers comfort and materials similar to a luxury saloon.

Compared to the already robust standard G550, the 4×4² offers more of every off-road specification: {{convert|7.9|in|cm|0|abbr=on}} of extra ground-clearance, {{convert|15.8|in|cm|0|abbr=on}} of additional wading depth, a 21.6-degree steeper approach-angle, 23.4° greater breakover-, and 13.4° extra departure-angle.<ref name=CnDblogSQ/> The front track is wider by {{convert|9|in|cm|0|abbr=off}}, the rear by {{convert|10|in|cm|0|abbr=off}}. The Mercedes 4×4² beats the [[Hummer H1]] on paper in almost every off-road measurement—except for traversing a slope. The 4×4² is limited to a 28.4° bank-angle, compared with the Humvee's 30°.<ref name=CnDblogSQ/>
